item.text:
Using your local prior for the structural baseline; I did not re-fetch the structured country-year indicators you already supplied.

Félix Tshisekedi was the constitutional head of state in 2022, with authority as guarantor of the Constitution, territorial integrity, and continuity of the state; he was also commander-in-chief, while the prime minister headed government and the president could proclaim a state of siege after consultation with the PM and the heads of both chambers. The practical constraints in 2022 were strong: an entrenched eastern conflict, the prolonged state of siege in Ituri and North Kivu, weak rule-of-law institutions, and dependence on regional mediation and military coordination rather than unconstrained executive control.

Your local prior already captures the inherited baseline well, so I am using it directly rather than searching again: persistent armed conflict and mass violence (`LF007`, `LF008`, `LF018`, `LF019`), severe repression and weak liberties (`LF009`-`LF024`), poor governance/corruption (`LF038`, `LF040`, `LF041`, `LF054`-`LF059`), and low development/service capacity (`LF042`-`LF053`).

Useful source families:
- Primary, legal: the DRC Constitution.
- Primary, presidential/favorable: `presidence.cd`.
- Independent, neutral/current-events: Reuters.
- Independent, local-language: Radio Okapi.
- Multilateral primary: UN Secretary-General and Security Council.
- Critical human-rights: Amnesty International and Freedom House.

Retained sources, with only the most useful cross-chapter set:

1. [Constitution de la République Démocratique du Congo](https://www.leganet.cd/Legislation/Constitution.htm) | Publisher: Leganet legal archive | Date: constitutional text adopted 2005, this page crawled recently | Precise fact: Article 69 makes the president head of state and guarantor of the Constitution; Articles 81, 83, and 85 cover senior appointments, commander-in-chief status, and proclamation of state of siege | Period fit: evergreen legal frame for 2022 | Ruler attribution: direct legal authority, not narrative attribution | Limitations: legal text does not show how power was exercised in practice | Contrary points: actual executive capacity was constrained by security breakdown and weak institutions, so formal authority overstates practical control.

2. [Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo - Présidence RDC](https://presidence.cd/president/le-president) | Publisher: Présidence RDC | Date: current official biography page; states he has been president since 24 Jan 2019 | Precise fact: confirms office, continuity, and official self-presentation of the presidency | Period fit: stable office status for 2022 | Ruler attribution: direct, primary, favorable | Limitations: self-authored institutional biography, not independent verification | Contrary points: does not address 2022 policy failures, conflict, or abuses.

3. [Adresse à la nation du Président de la République, Félix Tshisekedi suite à la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire à l’est du pays](https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/adresse_a_la_nation_du_president_de_la_republique_felix_tshisekedi_suite_a_la_deterioration_de_la_situation_securitaire_a_lest_du_pays) | Publisher: Présidence RDC | Date: 3 Nov 2022 | Precise fact: Tshisekedi publicly framed the eastern crisis as M23 aggression backed by Rwanda and said more than 200,000 people had fled Rutshuru-area fighting | Period fit: exact 2022 ruler statement during the M23 escalation | Ruler attribution: direct first-person attribution | Limitations: official framing, no neutral casualty verification in the text | Contrary points: Rwanda denies support; outside reporting and UN statements treat attribution as contested.

4. [Le mini-sommet de Luanda impose au m23/Rwanda un cessez-le-feu et le retrait des zones occupées en RDC](https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_mini-sommet_de_luanda_impose_au_m23rwanda_un_cessez_le_feu_et_le_retrait_des_zones_occupees_en_rdc) | Publisher: Présidence RDC | Date: 24 Nov 2022 | Precise fact: reports the Luanda mini-summit’s ceasefire, withdrawal, disarmament, and cantonment terms for M23 | Period fit: exact late-2022 peace-process milestone | Ruler attribution: direct but mediated through regional diplomacy | Limitations: government communiqué, not an implementation report | Contrary points: later reporting showed withdrawals were partial, fragile, and contested on the ground.

5. [RDC : Félix Tshisekedi annonce une table ronde sur l'état de siège](https://www.radiookapi.net/2022/05/05/actualite/securite/rdc-felix-tshisekedi-annonce-une-table-ronde-sur-letat-de-siege) | Publisher: Radio Okapi | Date: 5 May 2022 | Precise fact: reports Tshisekedi’s evaluation meeting on the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri and the plan for a roundtable on its future | Period fit: exact 2022 local-language reporting on an ongoing exceptional regime | Ruler attribution: indirect, but tied to a presidential meeting and government spokesperson | Limitations: radio report, brief on legal/political detail | Contrary points: Amnesty and other monitors argue the state of siege worsened repression rather than security.

6. [Nord-Kivu : reprise des combats entre FARDC et M23 à Kibumba](https://www.radiookapi.net/2022/11/20/actualite/securite/nord-kivu-reprise-des-combats-entre-fardc-et-m23-kibumba) | Publisher: Radio Okapi | Date: 20 Nov 2022 | Precise fact: records renewed fighting between FARDC and M23 near Kibumba, with civilians and local sources describing sustained hostilities | Period fit: exact 2022 field-level event in the core conflict zone | Ruler attribution: indirect; useful for the security environment under Tshisekedi | Limitations: situational reporting, not an attribution study | Contrary points: does not by itself prove presidential control or responsibility for battlefield outcomes.

7. [Heavy fighting as Congo tries to fend off resurgent M23 rebels](https://www.euronews.com/2022/05/27/us-congo-security) | Publisher: Euronews, Reuters content | Date: 27 May 2022 | Precise fact: reports heavy fighting in eastern Congo, including M23 gains near Goma and Kibumba | Period fit: exact 2022 onset of the major M23 offensive | Ruler attribution: indirect, independent chronology | Limitations: fast-moving news copy; relies on contemporaneous sources | Contrary points: later ceasefire and regional-force dynamics changed the tactical picture, so this is not the whole year.

8. [Congo expels Rwanda ambassador as M23 rebels capture strategic town](https://www.euronews.com/2022/10/30/congo-security) | Publisher: Euronews, Reuters content | Date: 30 Oct 2022 | Precise fact: reports Kinshasa expelled Rwanda’s ambassador after M23 seized Kiwanja and cut off Goma’s access to the upper province | Period fit: exact late-2022 escalation and government response | Ruler attribution: indirect, but directly about a decision taken by Tshisekedi’s government | Limitations: sourced through Reuters and official statements; battlefield control was still fluid | Contrary points: Rwanda denies support for M23; government claims of external aggression were disputed.

9. [Statement attributable to the Spokesman for the Secretary-General - on the Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://www.un.org/sg/en/content/sg/statements/2022-10-30/statement-attributable-the-spokesman-for-the-secretary-general-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-scroll-down-for-french-version) | Publisher: United Nations | Date: 30 Oct 2022 | Precise fact: UN said hostilities between FARDC and M23 had caused civilian casualties, massive displacement, and injury to four peacekeepers | Period fit: exact 2022 crisis snapshot | Ruler attribution: independent multilateral reporting, not presidential advocacy | Limitations: event-focused statement, not a full country assessment | Contrary points: the UN does not settle the political blame question and usually avoids adopting a single party’s full narrative.

10. [Security Council Press Statement on Situation in Democratic Republic of Congo](https://press.un.org/en/2022/sc15115.doc.htm) | Publisher: UN Security Council | Date: 22 Nov 2022 | Precise fact: the Council condemned M23’s renewed attacks and advance toward Goma and demanded withdrawal from occupied areas | Period fit: exact 2022 international reaction to the offensive | Ruler attribution: independent multilateral source | Limitations: press statement, not a detailed analytical report | Contrary points: does not by itself measure the Congolese government’s internal capacity or success.

11. [DRC: One year on, ‘State of Siege’ used as a tool to crush dissent](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/05/drc-one-year-on-state-of-siege/) | Publisher: Amnesty International | Date: 10 May 2022 | Precise fact: argues the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri had become a tool for arbitrary detention and suppression of critics rather than a security fix | Period fit: exact 2022 critique of the governing framework Tshisekedi kept in place | Ruler attribution: critical but directly relevant to presidential responsibility | Limitations: advocacy framing, strong emphasis on rights abuse | Contrary points: the government can plausibly argue it faced a real armed-insurgency emergency; Amnesty does not deny the underlying security crisis.

12. [Democratic Republic of the Congo: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/democratic-republic-congo/freedom-world/2023) | Publisher: Freedom House | Date: 2023 report covering 2022 developments | Precise fact: says the political system was paralyzed by elite manipulation, corruption was endemic, security remained tenuous, and the M23 offensive continued through 2022 | Period fit: retrospective 2022 synthesis with broad institutional coverage | Ruler attribution: critical, indirect, and system-level | Limitations: index/report format, not event-by-event sourcing | Contrary points: it compresses many dynamics into a single score narrative and is less useful for granular chronology than Reuters or the UN.

Compact event map for 2022:
- May: Tshisekedi kept the state of siege in Ituri and North Kivu under review; Amnesty argued it was being used against dissent rather than to restore security.
- May-June: the resurgent M23 offensive intensified around Rumangabo, Kibumba, and Goma’s approaches.
- July-August: regional mediation and the planned East African deployment became part of the response architecture.
- September-October: anti-UN and anti-Rwanda tensions rose; the east saw displacement, protests, and worsening military pressure.
- 30 Oct-3 Nov: M23’s gains triggered diplomatic escalation, including Rwanda’s ambassador being expelled and Tshisekedi’s national address blaming Rwanda-backed aggression.
- 22-24 Nov: UN and Security Council statements documented the deterioration; Luanda imposed ceasefire, withdrawal, disarmament, and cantonment terms.
- December: the year ended with continuing conflict, displacement, and contested implementation of the ceasefire framework.

- 1B: no retained source yet; your local prior already marks this chapter as no-evidence_found, so leave it empty unless you later want a narrow nuclear-capability search.

- 4B: use the Constitution, presidential bio, Freedom House, and the presidency’s 2022 speeches for office, mandate, and political constraints.
- 5B and 6B: your local prior is already the best base; no need to add external sources unless you want macroeconomic or health-system narrative color.
- 7B: use the Constitution, Amnesty, Freedom House, and the presidency’s anti-corruption/leadership framing only as self-claims, not proof.
- 8B: use the Constitution, presidential bio, UN statements, Freedom House, and the Luanda/UN material for state-capacity, diplomacy, and implementation constraints.
